Selects the type of noise being added to each frame

The number of Perlin noise octaves, that is the count of P-noise iterations. Higher values will make the noise more soft and smoke-like, whereas lower values will make it look more organic and spotty. It is limited by 8 octaves as the resulting gain will run out of bounds.

How much of noise from each octave is added on each iteration. Higher values will make it more straighter and sharper, while lower values will make it rounder and smoother. It is limited by 1.0 as the resulting gain fill the frame completely with noise.
The width of the Perlin sample. Lower values will make larger noise regions. Think of it as inverse brush stroke width. The greater this setting, the smaller details it will affect.
The height of the Perlin sample. Lower values will make larger noise regions. Think of it as inverse brush stroke width. The greater this setting, the smaller details it will affect.
The color coherence will attempt to sample the overall pixel color information, and trend those values analyzed in the first frame to be applied to future frames.

during the run sequence, only frames specified by this value will be extracted, saved, and diffused upon. A value of 1 indicates that every frame is to be accounted for. Values of 2 will use every other frame for the sequence. Higher values will skip that number of frames respectively.

when enabled, will re-extract video frames each run. When using video_input mode, the run will be instructed to write video frames to the drive. If you’ve already populated the frames needed, uncheck this box to skip past redundant extraction, and immediately start the render. If you have not extracted frames, you must run at least once with this box checked to write the necessary frames.

video_input mode only, enables the extraction and use of a separate video file intended for use as a mask. White areas of the extracted video frames will not be affected by diffusion, while black areas will be fully effected. Lighter/darker areas are affected dynamically.

Controls the contrast of the composite mask. 0.5 if half, 1 is normal contrast, 2 is double, etc.

If using autocontrast option, this is the low cutoff for the operation.

controls handling method of pixels to be generated when the image is smaller than the frame.
Perspective flip fv
the 2D vanishing point of perspective (recommended range 30-160)
HSV
HSV is a good method for balancing presence of vibrant colors, but may produce unrealistic results - (ie.blue apples)
LAB
LAB is a more linear approach to mimic human perception of color space - a good default setting for most users.
RGB
RGB is good for enforcing unbiased amounts of color in each red, green and blue channel - some images may yield colorized artifacts if sampling is too low.
Optical flow redo generation

This option takes twice as long because it generates twice in order to capture the optical flow from the previous image to the first generation, then warps the previous image and redoes the generation. Works in 2D/3D animation modes.
Redo
Diffusion Redo. This option renders N times before the final render. It is suggested to lower your steps if you up your redo. Seed is randomized during redo generations and restored afterwards.
MiDaS weight
sets a midpoint at which a depthmap is to be drawn: range [-1 to +1]
Sampling Mode
choose from Bicubic, Bilinear or Nearest modes. (Recommended: Bicubic)
Save depth maps
will output a greyscale depth map image alongside the output images.
